title: SEE ARKANSAS
governing_question: If every elected official disappeared tomorrow and we had to explain to a new group exactly how Arkansas presently functions—who governs, who pays, where the money goes, what Arkansas owns, what households experience, what Arkansas produces, and what it depends upon—could we do it?
finished_when: Answer to governing question is yes — via closed objects, not word count.

hierarchy: Official federal statistical series (Census, BLS, BEA, USDA, CMS, EIA, Fed as applicable)

progress.note: Blueprint % derives from object inventory (V2.1 ≈ 25% of blueprint when 152/152).

passes.name: People, Households & Place
passes.exit: Arkansas' people/place baseline + household archetype framework + geographic comparison framework.

passes.name: Government & Money
passes.exit: Arkansas Money Map + Government Function Map + Historical Budget Panel + dependency map.

passes.name: Production, Ownership & Capital
passes.exit: Production Map + Ownership Map + Capital Formation Map + External Dependency/Income baseline.

passes.name: Institutions, Power & Constraints
passes.exit: Arkansas Power Map + Authority/Constraint Matrix + federal/local dependency map.

passes.name: Whole-State X-Ray
passes.exit: ARKANSAS NOW — OPERATING X-RAY interactive join of 2.1.1–2.1.4.

geographic_dimension.decomposition_rule: Every baseline object capable of geographic decomposition must be evaluated for State → Region → County applicability. Not every metric needs county data. Every major system must ask whether geography materially changes the answer.
geographic_dimension.finish_line_addition: When V2.1 closes: Here's Arkansas—and here's how the Arkansas system manifests differently across its 75 counties.

passes_note: Geographic 75-county spine is permanent infrastructure inside SEE — populated field-first alongside passes 2.1.1–2.1.5, not as a sixth pass/gate.
